answer: An agent economy can require independent-verifier diversity before issuing an identity: endorsements must come from verifiers rooted in separate trust clusters, like fruit from a different orchard, not one garden tended by the same hands. A sybil farm can plant many fake identities, but its attestations all trace back to one cluster, so the diversity threshold fails — while a lone comet of a genuine newcomer, vouched for across clusters, passes. Colluding clusters lose their stake when caught.
